### Workflow

Input from SpawnWorkers
  ↓
HTTP POST: Wait for Workers Ready
  ↓
IF: All workers ready?
  ├─ YES: Continue
  └─ NO: Warn and continue anyway
  ↓
HTTP POST: Register Workers for Session
  ↓
Execute Workflow (Async): CoordinateBuild

### Wait Workers (Summary)
Polls worker health endpoints to verify they're online and ready to receive commands. It doesn't do any work itself—it just "knocks on the door" of each worker repeatedly until they answer or timeout.Think of it as: "Is anyone home? Is anyone home? Is anyone home?" (asks every 500ms until they respond or 30 seconds pass)

#### TL;DR
/api/orchestration/wait-workers = "Are all the worker processes actually online and responding to requests?"

Polls each worker's /api/health endpoint
Waits up to 30 seconds for them to respond
Checks every 500ms to be responsive
Checks in parallel (fast)
Returns success even if some fail (soft fail)
Used right after spawning to verify workers booted properly

It's the "health check before proceeding" step! ✅

### Create Session(Summary)
Creates a new tracking record for a multi-worker build project. It's essentially a "session bookmark" that stores metadata about a collaborative build, but doesn't spawn workers or do any actual work. It just registers the build in memory.

### Register Workers (Summary)

Links spawned workers to a build session. It's the "add these workers to this team/project" operation. This creates the association: "These 3 workers belong to build session XYZ"
Think of it as: "I have 3 workers and a build session. Connect them together."


####TL;DR

/api/orchestration/register-workers = "Associate these workers with this build session"

Requires: Session to exist (404 if not)
Does: Links workers list to session, updates statuses
Changes: Session status → workers_assigned, Worker status → assigned
Blocks: No (instant operation)
Used after: wait-workers (workers are ready)
Used before: reserve-location (need workers in session to position them)

It's the "Team formation" step! ✅
